open_issues: Wall discriminator not decided: the 1-minute load never met the frozen rule (bounded wait 21:57-22:17 used, load 12-28; other agents of the group and unpinned jobs of other projects, also on cores 6-11). One allowed measurement per cell is left; on a quiet host run in jacobian_assembly/: for each of the 5 cells './run_measurements.sh timing <cell> 3', then 'python3 -I build_results.py && python3 -I build_report.py' (NOTES.txt entry 5). Expected from the diagnostic numbers: dense PASS, wide band at the 1.5 threshold, narrow band KILL, so node rule FAIL (mixed) under the strict reading.

The strict node rule (every qualifying cell must pass) was declared before measuring; the narrow-band cell has an Amdahl bound below 1.5 by structure, so a node-level PASS was not reachable. Cell verdicts are reported separately so another reading can be recomputed.

rodas5p-integrators has no finite-difference state Jacobian; 'the protected driver's finite-difference path' is crates/vigilode/src/fd.rs (443-455, 476-509, 581-622), attached by the facade as a callback. The client re-implements that arithmetic; equality with the real code is shown only through vigilode::Rodas5p::solve in the standalone runner.

Fail-closed has a documented gap: the first-use check uses 8 sampled columns, so an undeclared entry aliased into a declared one in unsampled columns, or one whose finite difference is exactly zero at the checked state, is not detected. The sequential dense route has no check at all unless requested.
In a failed build the threaded modes have entered every right-hand side of the build, so rhs_calls is larger than in the sequential mode (the error returned and the trajectory are the same).

For bruss1d-n131072 about three quarters of this client's Jacobian phase is entry extraction and copying into the back end, not RHS time; threading cannot help there and a tighter sequential path was not built. Client construction (colouring, tables) costs 16-18 ms at n=4096 with 49 colours, 4-7% of the short timed solves.
vigilode Stats report jvp_calls = 0 for Jacobian::sparse_jvp on a banded pattern although the callback was called 368 times (outside this node's paths, not changed).

rulings: 'wall' of the frozen row: primary = whole solve (client construction including pool and colouring + the driver call); the Jacobian phase (TimedStageClient linearize_ns) is reported next to it and never used for PASS or KILL.

Cell verdict uses the best authoritative ratio over P in {2,4,6}; KILL needs all three authoritative and below 1.1. Node verdict: every qualifying cell must pass (strict reading), declared before measuring.

Run length of declared cells: 48 step attempts or the end of the span, the same in every arm and in the protected driver (bounds the time the timing lock is held without choosing a span from a trial run).
The first-use check (8 columns, plus one base evaluation with threads) is on in every timed arm; its right-hand sides are counted separately from the assembly count 'colours + 1'.

A violated pattern or a non-reproducible right-hand side returns CoreError::InvalidInput to the driver (fatal, run ends with Err); the typed AssemblyError is kept in AssemblyReportHandle because the driver drops the client on Err.
The third allowed timing measurement was not used on the loaded host; it is left for a quiet host instead of closing the cells with a third diagnostic_only measurement.
The qualifying problems were sized from operation counts only; no solver run or cost measurement preceded PREDECLARED.json.

findings.claim: Fail-closed PASS: a wrong pattern ends with a typed error and no silently wrong Jacobian (7 negative controls); the gap is limited to an aliased entry in unsampled columns.
findings.evidence: Reviewer probe with the default options (first-use check of 8 evenly spread columns, the setting of every timed arm), sequential and 3 workers. The builder's own ring problem declared tridiagonal (control 1 uses n = 12): fails closed for n = 12, 15, 33 (uncovered row) and n = 13, 14, 16, 32 (a sampled column hits); for n = 34, 64, 100, 127, 128, 1000 the run ends with success after 95, 44, 44, 44, 52, 46 accepted steps (28 with the true pattern), 4 Jacobian entries wrong at y0 (largest error 0.878), final state different in every component (9.3e-7 to 1.6e-6). The control passes at n = 12 only because n mod 3 = 0 leaves the corner rows uncovered. True Brusselator pattern minus one entry, build and default check at y0: n = 128: 48 of 508 not detected (9.4%); n = 1024: 497 of 4092 (12.1%); n = 131072: 26 of 201 sampled (12.9%). CheckColumns::All detected all of these except one whose finite difference is exactly zero at y0. A band declared one too narrow on the declared cells fails closed in 16 of 16 runs. For context, the facade's own banded finite-difference route accepts the same wrong ring declaration silently at n = 12, 64 and 1000, so the client is never less safe than the default path. Logs: review-scratch/logs/rv_probe_ring.log, rv_probe_deletion.log, rv_probe_deletion_large.log, rv_probe_narrow.log, rv_probe_facade_wrong.log.
findings.correction: Record the discriminator as: PASS on the 7 pre-declared controls only. With the default check the client does not fail closed for an omitted coupling that is aliased into a declared entry outside the 8 sampled columns (periodic ring with n >= 34 and n mod 3 != 0 declared as a band; 9-13% of single-entry omissions of the Brusselator pattern). Only CheckColumns::All, n extra right-hand sides at the first linearization, closed the cases tried. Do not describe the client as fail-closed without this qualifier. Whether the default becomes the full check is an owner decision.
